chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:
I heard him saying: 'If a man fasts Ramadan while traveling, it does not suffice for him, and he must repeat it.'

key_terms.الإِعَادَةُ: Repetition/Make-up (Qada), the requirement to fast again
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: Traveling/Journey, the state of being a traveler (musafir)
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan, specifically referring to the obligatory fast of Ramadan
key_terms.لَمْ يُجْزِهِ: It does not suffice/discharge the obligation

ai.seo_question: Does fasting while traveling in Ramadan count towards the obligatory fast, or must it be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the specific ruling for a traveler who chooses to fast during Ramadan, asserting that their fast is not valid and requires make-up (Qada). This view highlights a distinct juristic perspective within Shia scholarship regarding the permissibility and validity of fasting while traveling, contrasting with the more common view that the fast is valid but requires make-up. It underscores the importance of intention and adherence to the conditions of the fast for the obligation to be fully discharged.
